title: Catch and log exceptions around TutorPinService calls in the PIN entry/setup async handlers
why: _onPinComplete (gate) and _onConfirmPinEntered (setup) wrap their await in try/finally with no catch clause. TutorPinService.verifyTutorPin/setTutorPin only converts PinLockoutException — an underlying secure-storage failure (a real class of Android keystore/PlatformException issue this environment has hit before per the App Check debug-token flakiness on wipes) propagates as a raw, uncaught exception. Because _onPinComplete is invoked fire-and-forget (not awaited) from _appendDigit, the failure is swallowed by whatever global handler exists, with zero AppLogger call from this site and zero user feedback: _isVerifying resets to false in the finally block but _errorMessage stays null and _digits stays at 4 filled dots, leaving the user staring at a stalled numpad with no explanation and no way to retype until they notice backspace still works.
recommendation: Add a typed catch around the await that logs via AppLogger and sets a generic, localized _errorMessage (consistent with EH-2's 'no raw exception reaches presentation').
acceptance_criteria: _onPinComplete and _onConfirmPinEntered both have a catch block that calls AppLogger.instance.error and sets a localized _errorMessage
a test that makes the stubbed TutorPinService throw confirms the screen shows an error state instead of a silent stall

corrections: Minor: 'setTutorPin only converts PinLockoutException' overstates it — setTutorPin has zero exception handling (no lockout check exists for set), so it's worse than stated, not misleading in finder's favor.

EH-3's text addresses existing catch blocks that are empty/log-less; here there is no catch at all, so EH-2 (raw exception must not reach presentation) is the precise fit and alone fully supports the finding — citing EH-3 is a minor stretch, not a defect in the underlying claim.
